clauses.text:
By virtue of the authority vested in me  
as President of the United States and as  
Commander in Chief of the Army and  
Navy of the United States, it is hereby  
ordered that an Air Medal, with accom­
panying ribbons, be established for  
award to any person who, while serving  
in any capacity in the Army, Navy, Ma­
rine Corps, or Coast Guard of the United  
States subsequent to September 8, 1939,  
distinguishes, or has distinguished, him­
self by meritorious achievement while  
participating in an aerial flight.
The Air Medal and appurtenances  
thereto shall 'be of appropriate design  
approved by the Secretary of War, the  
Secretary of the Navy, and the Secre­
tary of the Treasury, and, under such  
regulations as said Secretaries may pre­
scribe, may be awarded by the Secretary  
of War, the Secretary of the Navy, or the  
Secretary of the Treasury, or by such  
commanding officers of the Army, Navy,  
Marine Corps, or Coast Guard as the  
said Secretaries may respectively desig­
nate. Awards to personnel of the Coast  
Guard when serving under his jurisdic­
tion shall be made by or under the direc­
tion of the Secretary of the Navy.
No more than one Air Medal shall be  
awarded to any one person, but for each  
succeeding meritorious achievement jus­
tifying such an award a suitable bar or  
other device may be awarded to be worn  
with the medal as prescribed by appro­
priate regulations. In the event of a  
posthumous award the medal, bar, or  
device may be presented to such repre­
sentative of the deceased as may be  
designated in the award.

Air M edal

Commander in Chief of the Army and  
Navy of the United States, it is hereby  
ordered that an Air Medal, with accom­
panying ribbons, be established for  
award to any person who, while serving  
in any capacity in the Army, Navy, Ma­
rine Corps, or Coast Guard of the United  
States subsequent to September 8, 1939,  
distinguishes, or has distinguished, him­
self by meritorious achievement while  
participating in an aerial flight.
The Air Medal and appurtenances  
thereto shall 'be of appropriate design  
approved by the Secretary of War, the  
Secretary of the Navy, and the Secre­
tary of the Treasury, and, under such  
regulations as said Secretaries may pre­
scribe, may be awarded by the Secretary  
of War, the Secretary of the Navy, or the  
Secretary of the Treasury, or by such  
commanding officers of the Army, Navy,  
Marine Corps, or Coast Guard as the  
said Secretaries may respectively desig­
nate. Awards to personnel of the Coast  
Guard when serving under his jurisdic­
tion shall be made by or under the direc­
tion of the Secretary of the Navy.
No more than one Air Medal shall be  
awarded to any one person, but for each  
succeeding meritorious achievement jus­
tifying such an award a suitable bar or  
other device may be awarded to be worn  
with the medal as prescribed by appro­
priate regulations. In the event of a  
posthumous award the medal, bar, or  
device may be presented to such repre­
sentative of the deceased as may be  
designated in the award.
F ranklin  D R oosevelt
The W hite  H ouse ,
May 11, 1942.

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register original (7 FR 3541, PDF page 1) is Executive Order 9158, Air Medal, signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt on May 11, 1942; number, title and date agree with the register row. The order has one inventory clause covering its three paragraphs. Later instruments naming it: EO 9242-A (September 11, 1942), which restated the first paragraph so that service in or with the Army, Navy, Marine Corps or Coast Guard qualifies, and EO 14085 section 1 (October 3, 2022), which further amended the first, second and third paragraphs (Armed Forces, Air Force and Space Force, Secretary of Defense design approval, Secretary of Homeland Security for the Coast Guard outside the Navy, and a new final paragraph on uniform regulations). Current law: the held U.S. Code note under 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, pt. II, ch. 57 (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints the order as amended by both instruments with no ending statement. No held instrument revokes or supersedes the order, so it is claimed in force on 2026-10-14.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Searched the held corpus for the order's number: the EDGES file of later-events, the U.S. Code note, and ten held texts naming it return only EO 9242-A and EO 14085 (both amendments) and an OFR See note to Transfer Order 30 of the Secretary of Defense dated December 10, 1948 (13 FR 8163), a cross reference whose text is not held and which is not described as an ending by any held source; EO 14085 amended the order in 2022, after that transfer order, and the Code note prints the order afterwards. The order has no duration, condition or sunset of its own, so no earlier own-terms end exists.","independent_command_check":"No independent command in the order was spent: the establishment of the medal, the award authority and the bar rule each continue under the order as amended (EO 14085 changed their wording but not their existence).","savings_check":"No clause ended and nothing was revoked, so there is no ended command whose awards or effects need saving; the order as amended remains the instrument establishing the Air Medal. The bounded searches name no ending.","scope_check":"One clause, the whole text of the order: the establishment of the Air Medal and ribbons, the design-approval and award authority of the Secretaries, and the one-medal-with-bars rule with posthumous presentation. All three paragraphs concern the same medal and none was separately ended or revoked."}

reviews.reasons: Quotes and hashes exact; identity (Roosevelt, May 11, 1942, Air Medal) agrees; the one-clause inventory is acceptable because all three paragraphs share one fate. EO 9242-A (first paragraph restated, 'in or with') and EO 14085 section 1 are correctly dated and the Code note shows the order current through release point 119-121 with no ending; the OFR See note to Transfer Order 30 (1948) is addressed and is not an ending. The outcome (operative) looks right, but the research rationale misstates what EO 14085 amended, asserting an amendment of the third paragraph that the source and the current Code text do not show, and contradicting the claim's own judgment_reason and later_events. Rejected for that factual error and inconsistency.
